prompt: Peitlyn decided that she would like to read more in 2026, so she made a resolution to read 30 minutes each day, starting January 1. If Peitlyn reads an average of 1 page every 2 minutes and she finishes her 6th book at the end of her reading session on March 31, 2026, what is the average number of pages per book for these six books?

solutions.title: Pages per day × days
solutions.body:
She reads $30 \div 2 = 15$ pages a day. January 1 through March 31, 2026 is $31 + 28 + 31 = 90$ days (2026 is not a leap year). Total pages $= 15 \times 90 = 1350$, so the average is $1350 \div 6 = 225$ pages per book.

**Answer: 225 pages**

solutions.title: Minutes first
solutions.body:
Total reading time: $90 \times 30 = 2700$ minutes, which is $2700 \div 2 = 1350$ pages. Per book: $1350 \div 6 = 225$.

**Answer: 225 pages**

prompt: Nora's resolution is to get more exercise. She decided that starting with the first full week in 2026, she will do a 45-minute workout four times each week (four days during every seven-day period). This means she will have to exercise four of the days during the week of Jan. 1 through Jan. 7, and then four of the days during the week of Jan. 8 through Jan. 14, etc. If Nora sticks to her resolution, what is the first possible date on which she could reach a total of 25 hours of exercise for the year?

solutions.title: Hours per week
solutions.body:
Each week she exercises $4 \times 45 = 180$ minutes $= 3$ hours. After 8 full weeks (starting Jan 1, 8, 15, 22, 29, Feb 5, 12, 19) she has 24 hours. The 9th week starts on February 26. To reach 25 hours as early as possible she works out on Feb 26 (24 h 45 min) and Feb 27 (25 h 30 min).

**Answer: February 27**

solutions.title: Count workouts
solutions.body:
25 hours $= 1500$ minutes, and $1500 \div 45 = 33\frac13$, so she needs 34 workouts. 8 weeks give 32 workouts, ending by Feb 25. Workouts 33 and 34 can be at the earliest on the first two days of the next week: Feb 26 and Feb 27.

**Answer: February 27**

prompt: Riley decided to cut back on the time that she spends watching television. During the first week of 2026 she will allow herself to watch her usual 22 hours of television. However, during each successive week of 2026, she will only allow herself to watch 90% of the time that she watched during the previous week. During which week (first, second, third, etc.) will her viewing time first be under 5 hours?

solutions.title: Geometric sequence
solutions.body:
Week $n$ allows $22 \times 0.9^{\,n-1}$ hours. We need $22 \times 0.9^{\,n-1} < 5$, i.e. $0.9^{\,n-1} < \frac{5}{22} \approx 0.227$.
$0.9^{14} \approx 0.2288$ (gives about 5.03 hours) and $0.9^{15} \approx 0.2059$ (about 4.53 hours). So $n - 1 = 15$ and $n = 16$.

**Answer: the 16th week**
